findings.F1: The tested effect is close to zero at every horizon. The 10-day slope of forward return (less the coin's mean) on the forecast is 0.000202 with t 0.37 over 1657 non-overlapping cases. At the other horizons the t is 0.20 at 5 days (3349 cases), 0.55 at 20 days (811) and -0.06 at 40 days (388). Using the raw 50/200 spread instead of the forecast gives t between -0.76 and 0.02.
findings.F2: Being in the up-cross state adds nothing at 10 days. The excess return is 0.00053 with the forecast above zero and -0.00054 with it at zero (Welch t 0.14, 832 vs 825 cases). The one-sample t of the "on" excess is 0.09. The share of positive returns while "on" is 2.1 points below the coin's usual share.
findings.F3: The null result is not hidden in one part of the data. Per-coin 10-day slope t ranges from -0.28 (XRP) to 0.94 (BTC). No year shows a positive t above 0.15, and two years are significantly negative: 2020 at t -2.22 and 2022 at t -2.42. Volatility terciles give t of -0.23, 0.54 and 0.15.
findings.F4: The effect does not grow with the spread or with how fresh the cross is. By forecast bucket, the 10-day excess is -0.0085, 0.0023, 0.0105 and 0.00004 for (0,5], (5,10], (10,15] and (15,20]. In the first 10 days after the cross it is 0.0038 (58 cases), against -0.037 at 10–30 days (89 cases).
findings.F5: What does carry the next 10 days is the coin's own recent move. The slope of the 10-day excess return on the coin's 20-day past return has t 2.80 over 1375 non-overlapping cases. Inside the top past-20-day tercile, the up-cross state also earns 0.0326 against -0.0067 off (t 2.34). Inside the bottom tercile it earns -0.0209 against 0.0097 (t -2.39). The moving-average state only matters through the recent move it partly overlaps with.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's own 20-day return, the more that coin rises over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader should lean long in proportion to a coin's recent 20-day gain rather than on its 50/200-day average spread, which by itself carried no edge.
ideas.name: twenty-day momentum continuation
